newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Horse Racing-NSW horse trainers head south.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-NSW horse trainers head south.

text.p: More than 700 trainers will leave New South Wales in the next three years to escape a government tax that is crippling the horse racing industry in the state.
That is the view of the New South Wales Trainers Association, which claims high wagering taxes are forcing their members to switch their operations to Victoria.
The Association says New South Wales racing industry is taxed at 52 per cent compared to 28 per cent in Victoria.
"The number of registered trainers in New South Wales has already fallen from 2,117 in September 1990 to 1,770 in September 1996," association president Mark Daniels said in a statement.
Increasing numbers of owners are taking their horses to Victoria, forcing trainers to follow, Daniels said.
"At this rate there will be as few as 1,000 trainers left in New South Wales by the year 2000 -- our numbers will have halved in a decade," he said.
The trainers are lobbying the New South Wales government to change its tax laws for the industry.
